Recommended Highlights This Week

1. In the Mood for Love in Concert – 24 and 25 October, Sands Theatre, Marina Bay Sands

2. Sacred Caves: Dunhuang, Buddhism, and the Silk Road – Asian Civilisations Museum, through 7 March 2027

3. teamLab: Infinite Existence – Supper House, Keppel Road, free, through 8 November

4. Golden Autumn Hairy Crab at Shang Palace – 15 October to 30 November

5. Moutai House – opening at The Fullerton Waterboat House, late October

Events & Festivals

Overall Summary

A quieter week for stadium concerts, with more for culture-minded guests. ONE OR EIGHT play Victoria Theatre on Wednesday 21 October, and at the weekend Marina Bay Sands hosts In the Mood for Love in Concert, with a live orchestra, on 24 and 25 October. BINI close the week at Arena @ EXPO on Sunday 25 October. Two exhibitions are worth steering guests to: Sacred Caves at the Asian Civilisations Museum, and teamLab: Infinite Existence at Supper House, which is free. Fan Chang Tien at the National Gallery and the PEACEMINUSONE × Toy Story pop-up at Clarke Quay, both opened last week, continue, and Little India's Deepavali lights remain on nightly ahead of Deepavali on Sunday 8 November.

In the Mood for Love in Concert

Wong Kar Wai's 2000 film is screened in restored full HD while the BASE Philharmonic Orchestra, conducted by Joshua Tan, performs Shigeru Umebayashi's score live, in sync with the picture.

Event Date: 24 October 2026, 2:00pm and 8:00pm; 25 October 2026, 1:00pm
Location: Sands Theatre, The Shoppes at Marina Bay Sands, 10 Bayfront Avenue
Admission: Ticketed via the Marina Bay Sands website, $68 to $158
Best For: Film Lovers / Classical and Orchestral Music Fans / Couples

Concierge Recommendation: A strong, easy recommendation for guests who want a refined evening or afternoon indoors at Marina Bay Sands, away from the crowds heading to the Singapore EXPO on Sunday.

ONE OR EIGHT – Special SHOW CASE 2026 in ASIA -V8-

The Japanese boy group bring their Asia showcase to Singapore for a single night at a seated venue.

Event Date: 21 October 2026, doors 7:00pm, show 7:30pm
Location: Victoria Theatre
Admission: Ticketed via Ticketmaster Singapore, seated, $88 to $138
Best For: J-pop and K-pop Fans

Concierge Recommendation: A mid-week option for guests who want a live show without a stadium crowd. Victoria Theatre is in the Civic District, so it is easy to reach from the hotel by taxi or MRT.

BINI: Signals World Tour 2026

BINI, the Filipino pop group, bring their Signals World Tour to Singapore on Sunday evening.

Event Date: 25 October 2026, 5:00pm
Location: Arena @ EXPO, Singapore EXPO
Admission: Ticketed via Ticketmaster, from $108 before booking fees
Best For: P-pop and K-pop Fans

Concierge Recommendation: An early-evening start, so guests can still have dinner afterwards. Advise allowing extra time for taxis and ride-hailing from the EXPO when the show ends.

Sacred Caves: Dunhuang, Buddhism, and the Silk Road

The Asian Civilisations Museum presents four life-size reproductions of the Mogao caves of Dunhuang, alongside paintings, sculptures, manuscripts, textiles and devotional objects. Cave 158, with its large reclining Buddha, is in the foyer, and three more caves are in the gallery.

Event Date: Now through 7 March 2027. Daily 10:00am–7:00pm; Fridays until 9:00pm
Location: Asian Civilisations Museum, 1 Empress Place
Admission: All-access ticket required. Singapore citizens and PRs $10; foreign residents and tourists $25 ($20 concession)
Best For: Culture-Minded Guests / Art and History Lovers

Concierge Recommendation: One of the strongest daytime recommendations in the city at the moment. Friday's late opening makes it a good pre-dinner stop, and it is a short walk from Raffles Place MRT.

teamLab: Infinite Existence

teamLab's first solo exhibition in Singapore is free to enter and is held on the fourth floor of Supper House on Keppel Road.

Event Date: Through 8 November 2026. Thursday to Saturday 12:00pm–7:00pm; Sunday 12:00pm–5:00pm; closed Monday to Wednesday
Location: Supper House, 37 Keppel Road, #04-02
Admission: Free
Best For: Art and Technology Fans / Families / Photography

Concierge Recommendation: A good free option for guests, but it is closed Monday to Wednesday, so this week it is only available from Thursday 22 October. Pair it with dinner in Tanjong Pagar.

Continuing This Week

Two exhibitions that opened last week are running through the coming days.

Fan Chang Tien: Rhythm of the Southern Brush – Wu Guanzhong Gallery, Level 4, City Hall Wing, National Gallery Singapore. Through 31 January 2027, daily 10:00am–7:00pm. General Admission ticket required; free for Singapore citizens and PRs.
Toy Story | PEACEMINUSONE: THE FIRST FAN pop-up – CQ @ Clarke Quay. Through 11 November 2026, daily 1:00pm–9:00pm. Entry passes $12; sold with pre-orders from the official website, with general sale to follow.

Concierge Recommendation: Fan Chang Tien pairs well with Sacred Caves on a Civic District day. The pop-up is a draw for BIGBANG and G-Dragon fans, who should check how to obtain a pass before they go.

Also This Week

  • Deepavali lights and Festival Village, Little India – lights nightly 7:00pm–midnight along Serangoon Road; Festival Village on Campbell Lane from 7:00pm, through 8 November. Free.

  • Halloween Horror Nights 14 – Universal Studios Singapore, Resorts World Sentosa. Thursday to Sunday, 7:30pm–12:30am, on select nights until 1 November. From $68.

  • Horizon of Khufu: Journey in Ancient Egypt – Parkview Square, 600 North Bridge Road. A VR experience, daily 10:00am–6:00pm, until 2 April 2027. $35 adult, $29 child under 8.

  • Singapore History Gallery – National Museum of Singapore. The reopened permanent gallery is open daily, 10:00am–7:00pm.

Restaurants & Bars

Moutai House

A three-storey Moutai destination in The Fullerton Waterboat House, bringing together an experiential centre, a Chinese restaurant run with the Imperial Treasure group, and a rooftop bar. The collection runs to more than 300 Moutai labels.

Location: The Fullerton Waterboat House, 3 Fullerton Road, Singapore 049215
Opening: Late October 2026; the exact date has not been confirmed
Experiential Centre: Daily 10:00am–10:00pm, covering Moutai’s history and production
Imperial Treasure Moutai House (second floor): Huaiyang and Guizhou cuisine. Daily 11:00am–3:00pm and 6:00pm–10:00pm
SOHAUS (rooftop bar, third floor): Tuesday to Saturday 5:00pm–midnight; signature Moutai cocktails with skyline and waterfront views
Reservations: Not yet released

Concierge Recommendation: Worth knowing about ahead of the opening, particularly for guests interested in baijiu or Chinese fine dining. Because the opening date is not confirmed, check moutaihouse.sg before booking on a guest's behalf.

Fico at Tanjong Beach Club

The second Fico restaurant, set on the beach at Tanjong Beach Club on Sentosa, with a focus on charcoal grilling and a lighter aperitivo-led spread. It opened on 28 September.

Location: Tanjong Beach Club, 120 Tanjong Beach Walk, Sentosa
Hours: Monday to Thursday 10:00am–8:00pm; Friday 10:00am–9:00pm; Saturday, Sunday and public holidays 9:00am–9:00pm
Reservations: +65 9750 5323

Concierge Recommendation: A relaxed beachside option for guests staying at Shangri-La Rasa Sentosa or heading to Sentosa for the day.

Dolpan Hwajoo

A Busan-style hotstone dining pub on Tanjong Pagar Road, serving makgeolli alongside Korean pub dishes.

Location: Level 1, 99 Tanjong Pagar Road, Singapore 088520
Hours: Sunday to Tuesday 11:00am–3:00pm and 5:00pm–midnight; Wednesday to Saturday 11:00am–3:00pm and 5:00pm–1:00am
Signature: Cheese Deunggalbi (pork ribs with flame-torched cheese), $48++; Dolpan Rose Daechang Dakbal, $46++; Perilla Oil Mak Guksu, $18++; makgeolli from $22++
Note: Not halal-certified. Several signature dishes use organ meats; the cheese ribs and noodle dishes are good alternatives

Concierge Recommendation: A lively evening option in Tanjong Pagar, pairing well with a visit to teamLab at Supper House on Keppel Road earlier in the day.

Special Mention: From Shangri-La’s Restaurant Recommendation List

One pick this week from Shangri-La Singapore's own curated list of recommended restaurants across the city:

Sabai Fine Thai on the Bay

Sabai Fine Thai grew from a belief that the distinctive flavours of Thai food would be appreciated all around the world. In the kitchen, Chef Samlee embodies that philosophy: more than thirty years ago, as a former cook for Thai royalty, she cooked for HRH Princess Srinagarindra, the Princess Mother of King Rama IX, and has spent her career perfecting her cooking.

Address: #01-02 Customs House, 70 Collyer Quay, Singapore 049323

Telephone: +65 6535 3718

Website: https://www.sabaifinethai.com.sg/

Concierge Recommendation: A good option for guests who want Thai cuisine in the Raffles Place and Collyer Quay area, with a waterfront setting. Reserve by telephone.

Hotel & Hospitality News

No new hotel openings or leadership appointments to report this week. For reference, DoubleTree by Hilton Singapore Robertson Quay opened on 30 September (covered in Edition 016), and its all-day restaurant, SAUS, opens on 1 November.

Transport & Operational Updates

Road closures for the Formula 1 Singapore Grand Prix have now lifted, and no Woodsville Tunnel closures fall in this edition's window. Overnight works run on several expressways, typically 12:00am to 5:00am: the KPE tunnel slip roads on 19, 20, 21 and 24 October, the MCE slip roads on 22 and 23 October, and the Sentosa Gateway Tunnel slip road on 19 October for tunnel washing. Bridge works on the TPE and PIE slip roads towards Tampines Avenue 7 and Loyang Avenue run from 10:00pm to 5:30am on 21 to 25 October.

Weekend road closures to note: Holland Village is partially closed Monday to Thursday and fully closed Friday to Sunday, 6:30pm to 2:30am; Liang Seah Street is closed Friday to Sunday, 6:30pm to midnight. In Little India, Lembu Road, Kerbau Road, Chander Road, Dunlop Street and Birch Road are closed on Sunday 25 October from 12:00pm to midnight, so guests going to see the Deepavali lights should be dropped off nearby. In Kampong Gelam, Bussorah Street and Baghdad Street are closed on Saturday and Sunday, and Haji Lane and Bali Lane daily.

Expect higher ride-hailing demand around Singapore EXPO on Sunday 25 October for BINI (5:00pm), and around Marina Bay Sands on 24 and 25 October for In the Mood for Love in Concert.

Suggested Itineraries

A Silk Road Day in the Civic District

Morning: Start at the Asian Civilisations Museum for Sacred Caves and the life-size Mogao cave reproductions.

Afternoon: Walk to the National Gallery Singapore for Fan Chang Tien: Rhythm of the Southern Brush, open daily until 7:00pm.

Evening: Dinner at Shang Palace for the Golden Autumn Hairy Crab menu.

Tip: On Friday the Asian Civilisations Museum stays open until 9:00pm, so the order can be reversed if guests prefer to see the Gallery first.

A Tanjong Pagar Afternoon and Evening

Afternoon: Visit teamLab: Infinite Existence at Supper House on Keppel Road (free; Thursday to Saturday 12:00pm–7:00pm).

Evening: Dinner at Dolpan Hwajoo on Tanjong Pagar Road, which reopens for dinner at 5:00pm.

Tip: teamLab is closed Monday to Wednesday, so this plan works from Thursday 22 October.

A Weekend Evening at Marina Bay Sands

Saturday: In the Mood for Love in Concert at Sands Theatre, 2:00pm or 8:00pm.

Sunday: The 1:00pm performance of In the Mood for Love works well as a matinee, leaving the evening free for dinner.

Tip: A good alternative to the stadium and EXPO concerts for guests who prefer a quieter, more refined outing.

Quick Reference

Best Refined Evening Out: In the Mood for Love in Concert (Sands Theatre, 24 and 25 October)

Best Exhibition: Sacred Caves (Asian Civilisations Museum, through 7 March 2027)

Best Free Pick: teamLab: Infinite Existence (Supper House, Thursday to Sunday, through 8 November)

Best Concert This Week: BINI (Arena @ EXPO, 25 October) or ONE OR EIGHT (Victoria Theatre, 21 October)

Best Hotel Dining Pick: Golden Autumn Hairy Crab at Shang Palace (from 15 October)

Best New Opening: Moutai House (The Fullerton Waterboat House, late October)

Looking Ahead: The Rose at The Star Theatre on 27 October; Interstellar – Live at The Star Theatre on 31 October; Deepavali on Sunday 8 November
